title: Variation of g Due to Altitude and Depth
topicTitle: Variation in value of 'g' due to altitude and depth
notes: **At altitude $h$:** $g' = g\left(\frac{R}{R+h}\right)^2$. As height increases, $g$ decreases because distance from Earth's centre increases.
**At depth $d$:** only the mass within radius $(R-d)$ contributes to gravity. $g' = g\left(1 - \frac{d}{R}\right)$. At the centre ($d=R$), $g=0$.
**Why depth reduces $g$ linearly:** the outer shells cancel by symmetry; only the inner sphere pulls inward, and its mass decreases as $d$ increases.
**Why altitude reduces $g$ quadratically:** the inverse-square law dominates; even a small increase in $r$ causes a noticeable drop in $g$.
**Practical note:** $g$ at Mount Everest ($\approx 9.77\,\text{m/s}^2$) is slightly less than at sea level ($\approx 9.83\,\text{m/s}^2$).
